tier_reason: Upgraded from C to A. The raw_data.txt page lists the per-run Tokio, Glommio and Monoio QPS, with Tokio 4C(1K) at 434565, Glommio at 603016 and Monoio at 810075. The page and docs/en/benchmark.md give the CPU (Xeon Gold 5118), the kernel and the compiler (rust nightly-2021-11-26). The benchmark code is public in monoio-rs/monoio-benchmark (monoio-server/, tokio-server/, glommio-server/, client/), and its Cargo.toml [profile.release] sets lto = true and the README runs target/release binaries, so the flags are stated too.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: rust nightly-2021-11-26; cargo release build (target/release) with [profile.release] lto = true, debug = false, overflow-checks = false (monoio-rs/monoio-benchmark Cargo.toml)
corrections.hardware: Intel Xeon Gold 5118 @ 2.30GHz, Intel X710 10GbE SFP+ NIC, Linux 5.15.4-arch1-1; client and server on separate physical machines on the ByteDance production network
corrections.claimed_speedup: 4-core server, 1KB messages, peak QPS: Monoio 810,075 vs Tokio (epoll) 434,565 (~1.86x, derived from page data) and vs Glommio (io_uring) 603,016 (~1.34x, derived from page data). At 16 cores with 100B messages, Monoio peaks at 2,802,033 vs Tokio 917,419 (~3.05x, derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark by the Monoio maintainers, run in late 2021 on Linux 5.15. The benchmark code (monoio-rs/monoio-benchmark) and the raw numbers are public. The docs say that with 1 core and few connections, Tokio has lower latency and higher throughput than Monoio. The comparison is between runtimes (Tokio's mio/epoll reactor) and not raw epoll. The GitHub repo moved from bytedance/monoio to monoio-rs/monoio (the old URL redirects). The benchmark repo's workspace takes monoio from git and uses a nightly rust-toolchain, so a re-run today would not use the 2021 versions exactly.

notes: All claimed numbers match raw_data.txt exactly. The license is dual MIT OR Apache-2.0: monoio/Cargo.toml says so and both LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE exist, although the GitHub API reports only Apache-2.0. The repo moved to the monoio-rs org; consider updating repo_url to https://github.com/monoio-rs/monoio. Stars 5117, last commit 2026-05-29, not archived, not a fork.

tier_reason: First-party page with Photon and boost::asio rows in the same streaming and ping-pong tables. The numbers match. Only Photon's own test program (examples/perf/net-perf.cpp) is published, not the boost::asio server. The compiler and flags are not stated beyond CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, and the CPU is given only as 'Intel Platinum CPU 2.70GHz' with no model number, so the record falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Ping-pong (1,000 conns, 512B): Photon 412K QPS / 1.57Gb vs boost::asio 393K QPS / 1.49Gb (~1.05x, derived from page data); streaming (4 conns, 512B): Photon 1604K QPS / 6.12Gb vs boost::asio 634K QPS / 2.42Gb (~2.5x, derived from page data)
corrections.hardware: Cloud VMs for server and client, 64 cores, 128GB RAM, 'Intel Platinum CPU 2.70GHz' (exact CPU model not stated), Linux kernel 6.x, 32Gb network bandwidth; per-core test with thread count limited to 1
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark. Only Photon's test program (examples/perf/net-perf.cpp; default socket type tcp on the default epoll engine) is published, and the boost::asio echo server code is not. The CPU model number, compiler and optimization flags are not stated, only a CMake Release build. The test measures single-thread (per-core) QPS on cloud VMs. In the ping-pong test the win over boost::asio is small (~1.05x). The same page also shows Photon at 114K QPS vs Nginx (1 worker) at 97K QPS when serving 4KB static files.

notes: All claimed numbers match the page (docs source doc/docs/performance/network-performance.md), and both ratios check out (412/393 = 1.05x, 1604/634 = 2.53x). The README lists production users Alibaba, Ant Group, ByteDance, Xiaomi and XSKY, and projects such as overlaybd and OSSFSv2. Metadata is correct: Apache-2.0, 1232 stars, last commit 2026-09-25, not archived, not a fork.

tier_reason: The first-party README table has FastAPI (REST and WebSocket), gRPC and UCall rows on AWS c7g.metal (Graviton 3), and all the quoted numbers appear there. The code is public (examples/login/*, examples/bench.py) and CMakeLists.txt sets Release -O3. The compiler version is not stated, the README's reproduce link (tree/dev/examples/sum) is dead, and the measured 'sum' example was later refactored into examples/login, so the record falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table: UCall io_uring (C server, connection reused) 22us / 231,000 rps vs FastAPI over REST (no connection reuse) 1,203us / 3,184 rps (~55x latency, ~72x throughput, derived from page data). Vs FastAPI over WebSocket (connection reused) 86us / 11,356 rps: ~3.9x latency, ~20x throughput (derived from page data). A closer like-for-like pair is UCall io_uring with a Python server, at 40us / 210,000 rps: ~2.2x latency and ~18x throughput vs FastAPI WebSocket (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build with -O3 (CMakeLists.txt default). The compiler version is not stated; the reproduce steps in examples/login/README.md install g++ via apt. FastAPI/uvicorn versions are not stated.
corrections.hardware: AWS c7g.metal (Graviton 3), Ubuntu 22.10 AMI, Linux kernel 5.19; throughput clients run on the same machine as the server
corrections.caveats: Cross-language, cross-framework comparison (C or Python-bound UCall vs a Python FastAPI/uvicorn app), not a controlled event-loop shootout. The ~55x/~72x headline pairs a connection-reusing UCall server with FastAPI REST, which does not reuse connections. The like-for-like WebSocket pair gives ~3.9x latency and ~20x throughput. The numbers date from Feb-Mar 2023 and were measured on a 'sum' endpoint. That example was refactored into examples/login on 2023-03-21, and the README's reproduce link (tree/dev/examples/sum) is now dead. A cleaner internal comparison is UCall's POSIX backend (src/engine_posix.cpp: blocking accept/recv, no epoll) at 62us / 79,000 rps vs the io_uring backend at 22us / 231,000 rps (~2.8x). That baseline is blocking sockets, not epoll.

notes: The numbers are exact and the ratios check out (1203/22 = 54.7x, 231000/3184 = 72.5x, 86/22 = 3.9x, 231000/11356 = 20.3x). The record's language 'C' is loose: the engines are C++ (src/engine_posix.cpp, src/engine_uring.cpp) behind a C API, plus Python bindings. Metadata is correct: Apache-2.0, 1334 stars, last commit 2025-09-16 (just over 12 months ago, so stale), not archived, not a fork.
